key_insight: Ti3C2Tx MXene stability in perovskite precursor inks depends on the chemical environment: iodine and polyiodides accelerate degradation, PbI2 causes slower oxidation, and MAI provides surface passivation.
engineering_relevance: Controlling precursor composition and addition order could help preserve or tune MXene surfaces during perovskite solar-cell fabrication.
method: Expose MXenes to individual and combined MAPbI3 precursor components.
Use X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy to characterize chemical and surface changes.
Apply density functional theory to investigate surface interactions.
evidence_signal: Combined XPS and DFT results support distinct oxidation and passivation mechanisms, though the abstract reports no quantitative stability or device-performance metrics.
watch_item: Addition order changes the MXene surface state, so processing protocols require careful validation; these findings concern a model MAPbI3 precursor system.
paper_title: Dynamic Chemical Changes of Ti3C2Tx MXenes in Halide Perovskite Precursor Environments
